name: Change Audit — FortiGate Firewall Configuration Changed
description:
Change objective
Audit configuration changes on the FortiGate perimeter firewalls (add/edit/move/delete of policy, objects, routes, VPN, profiles) for change control — perimeter config changes can open access or weaken defenses.

Detection logic
FortiGate emits a configuration event for each administrative change, naming the config path/object and the administrator. This rule surfaces all firewall config changes as an auditable change feed.

Why this works
The FortiGate config-change action and path fields are structured and attributed to an admin, giving a clean change-audit trail for the perimeter.

False positives
Routine authorized firewall administration and policy tuning.

Tuning
Correlate each change with a change ticket; escalate changes that add allow rules, modify NAT/VPN, or touch admin accounts; allowlist sanctioned automation.

Required telemetry
FortiGate config log: fortinet.firewall.action (Edit/Add/Move/Delete), cfgpath/cfgobj/cfgattr (what changed), fortinet.firewall.ui / user (administrator).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation / audit guide
1. fortinet.firewall.action = the change; cfgpath/cfgobj = what changed; ui/user = the administrator.
2. Verify against change control; a new allow policy, NAT/VPN change, or admin-account change is higher priority.
false_positives: Routine authorized firewall administration and policy tuning.
query: fortinet.firewall.action:("Edit" or "Add" or "Move" or "Rename") or (fortinet.firewall.action:"Delete" and fortinet.firewall.cfgpath:*)
